name: Netlex
tagline: Contract lifecycle management and legal workflow platform aimed at Brazilian legal departments and law firms.

pricing.notes: Enterprise legal software, pricing is quote-based and not published. No number asserted.

verdictSummary: You can absolutely build a contract folder with metadata, renewal dates, and email reminders in an afternoon. That is not what anyone is buying here. CLM gets paid for approval chains that hold up in an audit, immutable version history, signature trails, clause libraries the legal team actually agreed on, and integrations into ERP and e-signature providers. The moment a contract dispute or an auditor shows up, your SQLite file is evidence of nothing. If you are one person tracking your own contracts, build the tracker; if you are a legal department, the thing you need is the part that is boring and regulated.
coreLoopDIY: A local contract repository: upload PDFs, tag counterparty, value, effective and expiry dates, and get email nudges before renewal or termination windows close.
requirements: Local machine or small VPS to run it
Somewhere to actually keep the signed PDFs backed up
whatYouLose: Audit-grade version history and who-approved-what trails
Multi-step approval workflows across legal, finance, and the business unit
Native e-signature integration and the signature evidence package that comes with it
Clause libraries, templates, and automated drafting from approved language
ERP, CRM, and SSO integrations, plus the data residency and LGPD paperwork enterprise buyers ask for
moatNotes: Brazilian legal ops has its own gravity: local signature law, LGPD, court and ERP integrations, and buyers who need a vendor to point at when something goes wrong.
whyPeopleStillPay: Legal departments do not buy a database, they buy defensibility. The value is that fifteen people in three departments can route a contract through a defined approval path, that every edit is attributable, that the signature is legally sound in the relevant jurisdiction, and that a vendor with a contract and a support line is accountable for all of it. A personal build gives you storage and reminders, which is the easy 10 percent. The hard 90 percent is the workflow everyone has agreed to follow and the audit trail that proves they did.
notes: A contract shelf with deadline alarms is a one-sitting build; a defensible approval trail is not. The moat is compliance plus the multi-department workflow everyone has already been trained to follow.
prompt:
Build a local contract repository and deadline tracker. Single user, runs on my machine, no cloud accounts.

Stack, no substitutions:
- Next.js (App Router, TypeScript) with Tailwind
- SQLite via better-sqlite3, file at ./data/contracts.db
- Uploaded PDFs stored on disk at ./data/files, never in the DB
- node-cron inside a small standalone worker script for reminders
- nodemailer for email, SMTP creds from .env

Data model: contract (title, counterparty, type, status [draft, in_review, signed, expired, terminated], currency, value, effective_date, expiry_date, notice_period_days, auto_renew boolean, owner_note), file (contract_id, original filename, stored path, sha256, uploaded_at), event (contract_id, kind, note, created_at) as an append-only activity log.

Pages:
- / : table of contracts, sortable, filter by status and counterparty, color the rows where expiry or notice deadline is inside 60 days
- /contracts/new : form with PDF upload, multiple files allowed
- /contracts/[id] : all fields editable, file list with download links, activity log appended on every save, free-text notes
- /calendar : simple month grid of expiry and notice-window dates

Reminder worker (scripts/remind.ts, run via npm run remind): finds contracts where expiry_date minus notice_period_days falls within the next 30 days, sends one digest email, writes a reminder row to event so it never double-sends for the same window.

Also include: CSV export of all contracts, and a /api/health route.

Explicitly out of scope, do not build: e-signature, user accounts, roles, approval workflows, OCR, AI clause extraction, multi-tenant anything.

Secrets in .env.example: SMTP_HOST, SMTP_USER, SMTP_PASS, REMINDER_TO. No telemetry, no external calls except SMTP. Seed script with 8 fake contracts spread across statuses. README with setup in under ten lines.
